def min_weighted_completion(parent, t, w):
    """Schedule dependent jobs on one machine to minimize total weighted completion time.

    There are n jobs, numbered 0..n-1 (1 <= n <= 200). Job i takes t[i]
    time units (1 <= t[i] <= 10**6, int) and has weight w[i]
    (0 <= w[i] <= 10**6, int). parent[i] is either -1 (job i has no
    prerequisite) or an int with 0 <= parent[i] < i, meaning job
    parent[i] must be completed before job i starts. The prerequisite
    links therefore form a forest of rooted trees.

    A schedule runs all n jobs one at a time, back to back, starting at
    time 0, with no idle time and no preemption, in any order that
    respects every prerequisite. If job i finishes at time C_i, the cost
    of the schedule is the sum over all i of w[i] * C_i.

    Return the minimum possible cost over all valid orders, as an int.
    The returned value is a unique minimum, so no output tie-breaking is
    needed. len(parent) == len(t) == len(w) == n. Weights may be 0;
    durations are always >= 1; n == 1 is valid.

    >>> min_weighted_completion([-1], [3], [7])
    21
    >>> min_weighted_completion([-1, -1, 0], [5, 4, 1], [1, 4, 100])
    645
    >>> min_weighted_completion([-1, 0, 1], [2, 3, 4], [5, 1, 2])
    33
    """
